prs.title: chips: rp2040: PIO cleanups

commits.messageHeadline: chips: rp2040: pio: retire the examples module

prs.thread:
### What this does

One change to the RP2040 PIO driver.

This PR has shrunk three times. It opened as five commits. Two went after
@ppannuto's review, which was right that they replaced concrete hardware types
with numbers. A third went after @bradjc asked what the file moves accomplish.
The fourth goes now, at @ppannuto's request: the RP2350 pad controls have
nothing to do with the PIO cleanup, and belong in a GPIO PR of their own. That
PR is next, and the comment below has the measurement behind it.

**Retire `mod examples` in `pio.rs`.** A private module whose methods were all
`pub`, so API rather than examples, documented as being for
`pico_explorer_base`, which has not used it for some time. Three of its eleven
methods have callers and move next to them; the other eight have none in chips,
boards, capsules, kernel or libraries. `cyw43_spi_program_init` is the one worth
relocating on its own: it sets drive strength, slew rate and Schmitt triggers
for the half-duplex gSPI bus, which the generic PIO API does not expose, and it
sat in the middle of the PIO driver rather than with the gSPI driver that needs
it.

`impl RPGpio { fn from_u32 }` goes with them. `RPGpio` is already declared
inside `enum_from_primitive!`, so the inherent method was shadowing
`FromPrimitive::from_u32` with thirty numbered arms and a panicking wildcard.
Callers use `expect` rather than `unwrap`, which keeps the valid range in the
panic message where the inherent method had it. `pio.rs` loses 272 lines.

### Testing Strategy

Rebased onto `479b61829` and rebuilt from scratch. The four RP2040 boards are
unchanged in text, data and bss, compared mechanically rather than by eye:

    board                  text   data     bss   linked .text
    raspberry_pi_pico     98348      0   16528   byte-identical
    pico_explorer_base   102444      0   72668   byte-identical
    nano_rp2040_connect   94252      0   14368   byte-identical
    raspberry_pi_pico_w  352300      0   20724   differs, see below

Two builds of the base produce identical bytes, so the difference below is not
build noise.

On `raspberry_pi_pico_w`, the only board using the gSPI initialiser,
`RPGpio::from_u32` disappears (44 bytes) and the `expect` path brings in
`Option::expect` (16), `expect_failed` (24) and `panic_display::<&str>` (28).
`start` grows 36 bytes where they inline. Alignment absorbs the difference, so
text is unchanged.

These are the numbers from the previous push rather than a fresh run. The
commit is unchanged in content and sits on the same base; the commit that came
off touched one file, `chips/rp2350/src/gpio.rs`, which no RP2040 board
compiles. The RP2350 boards are no longer in the table because no RP2350 file
is in the diff any more.

I do not have an RP2040, so none of this has been on one, and the link
comparison above is the whole of the evidence.

### My own review

The retained commit is unchanged in content from the version I read before the
last push. I have not built this rebase or run any of it on hardware.

### AI disclosure

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`: written and then trimmed with Claude Code (Claude
Opus 5). The retained commit is unchanged in content from the previous push.
Every number quoted above was measured rather than recalled, on the push noted.


Full context: 
https://via-balaena.github.io/tock-rp2350/
 ␟ You're right, and I've dropped both commits. The arithmetic that replaced the
`TREQ_SEL` table is gone, and `set_pins` and `set_input_sync_bypass` take
`&RPGpioPin` again. What's left is the three you hadn't reached, none of which
erase a type or depend on anything shared.

On the larger point: understood, and `chips/nrf52840` is the model I should
have started from. Neither `Pio` nor `StateMachine` ever stores a pin type, so
keeping the concrete types across the move costs almost nothing. The move
needs `chips/rp2xxx` from #5112, so it's out of this PR rather than stacked.

One thing your comment turned up: `rx_fifo_addr` and `tx_fifo_addr` recompute
an address from a hardcoded chip base *and* take a `PIONumber` alongside a
state machine that already knows its block, so the two can disagree. That
belongs with the move.
 ␟ The changes to rp2350 look fine to me.

For the PIO changes, what does moving the functions to different files accomplish? ␟ I just clicked merge on #5112, so the point is a bit moot now, but stacked PRs are fine (preferred even) — in the future you can have this PR target the branch from #5112 and then tell github it's stacked, and github will automatically retarget this to master when #5112 is moved ( https://github.github.com/gh-stack/ ).

It's a newer feature in github, but fits very well with our workflow, and helps keep reviews contained/focused when multiple dependent things are in flight. ␟ `gpio_init` shouldn't have been in this PR, and I've dropped it. It never
changed files anyway: it left `impl Pio` for a free function in the same file,
because it's the only method on `Pio` that names `GpioFunction`, and the two
chips don't share that enum. That's preparation for moving `Pio` into `rp2xxx`
and nothing else, and with #5112 merged that PR can be written now, so it
belongs there where the reason is visible in the diff.

The other commit is a deletion rather than a move. Eight of the eleven methods
in `mod examples` have no caller anywhere in the tree; the three that do have
exactly one caller each, so they moved next to it instead of staying in a
module named `examples`. `pio.rs` loses 272 lines.

Rebased onto master: two commits, +170/-280, sizes unchanged on all five
boards.
 ␟ @ppannuto 

One catch: GitHub's docs say cross-fork stacks aren't supported, so a PR from
`via-balaena` can't target another of my own branches. That fits what's here,
where every stacked PR is from a `tock/tock` branch and no fork PR has a base
other than `master`, which is probably why it hasn't come up.

Not a problem for PR 2, which can wait for this one and rebase onto master.
Worth asking only if you'd rather review it stacked, since its base branch
would then need to live in `tock/tock`.
 ␟ re cross-fork stacks: Ah, too bad. I'm used to reviewing stacks "manually", as long as PR descriptions are clear about which commits are relevant, we'll have to keep doing that. ␟ @ppannuto Dropped. One commit left.

**The enums: yes.** `SlewRate` and `DriveStrength` are identical across the two
chips, character for character, down to `DriveStrength`'s inconsistent spelling
(`Drive2mA`, then `Drive4ma`, `Drive8ma`, `Drive12ma`). They go into `rp2xxx`,
re-exported from both.

**The rest: more different than it looks.** The two files are 723 and 1589
lines, but that gap is almost all register map. The logic below is 425 lines
against 419, and normalising the chip names, `diff` reports 70 changed lines.
All 70 are silicon:

- `GpioFunction` has `PIO2` and `XIP` where the RP2040 has `GPCK`, pushing
  `USB` from 9 to 0xa
- the RP2350 clears pad isolation, `GPIO_PAD::ISO`, on activation. The RP2040
  has no such field
- the RP2040 carries the RP2040-E5 USB errata workaround, `start_usb_errata`
  and `finish_usb_errata`
- the SIO fields are `GPIO_OE::OE` and `GPIO_OUT::OUT` on one chip,
  `GPIO_OE::GPIO_OE` and `GPIO_OUT::GPIO_OUT` on the other, for the same bits

A shared `RPGpioPin` is reachable, but it is four decisions rather than a move.
My plan is the enums and the three missing pad methods first, consolidation as
its own PR on top. Say if you would rather see it in one go.
 ␟ @bigmark222 can you please rewrite the pull request description using the template in https://github.com/tock/tock/blob/master/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md ␟ Please note @bigmark222, from the CONTRIBUTING.md file:

> Neither the pull request description nor any subsequent PR comments are allowed to be written using AI (exception: tools used exclusively for accessibility or translation are acceptable). Large Language Models often make unverified claims and produce verbose output. Writing PR comments by hand reduces cognitive burden for reviewers, incentivizes authors to reflect on generated changes, and keeps communication succinct. If including AI output genuinely serves the purposes of the PR, include it in a [\<details\>](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details) drawer. ␟ Why do we want to get rid of examples like `hello_program_init`? That seems like a useful test/sample/demo. ␟ Thanks for the review.

The four `*_program_init` functions (`blinking_hello`, `blink`, `sideset`, `hello`) have no corresponding PIO program in the tree today. The bytes were removed in commit `6b9e776e5` (October 2024, PR #4179). Unlike the three kept functions (`pwm`, `spi`, `cyw43_spi`) where the driver file supplies the program bytes, these four depended on the board code that's now gone. `hello_program_init` pushes `0b11000000` into a FIFO for a program that isn't there. The parameters do get passed to `gpio_init` and `set_pins_dirs`, but the mask is fixed, so the driven pins don't follow `pin1`/`pin2` (default: pins 6 and 7; with non-default `out_pins_base`, base+6 and base+7). The commented-out board call passed 6 and 7.

These were commented out before the PIO PR merged; only `pwm_program_init` was live at `6b9e776e5^`. None of the eight functions have callers on master today (verified by `git grep -nw`).

The `read_*` debug helpers are different. They're plain register reads that don't need a program loaded and are genuinely useful for bring-up. I can keep those and delete only the four `*_program_init` functions if you prefer. If I keep them, I'd lift them into the top-level `impl Pio` block (the one ending just above line 1677) and remove `mod examples` entirely.

The original examples are recoverable from `6b9e776e5^`. The assembled bytes are still in that commit. Restoring them properly would mean putting the board-side code back, and testing on RP2040 hardware, which I don't have. That's better as a follow-up.

Let me know if you want me to keep the `read_*` helpers. I'll update the PR title to `"chips: rp2040: PIO cleanups"` either way.  ␟ I'm thoroughly confused. I guess the tests were added to the chip crate in one PR, used in a different PR for testing, but reverted from the second PR's main.rs changes before the second PR was merged.

I guess I'm fine with whatever in this case. It doesn't seem like there is a clear testing/bring up strategy for the rp2x PIO. ␟ @bradjc 

You were right:

- Tests added to chip crate in one PR, used in another, reverted from `main.rs` before merge.
- Evidence: at `6b9e776e5^`, 5 `program_init` calls, 4 commented out, 1 live (`pwm_program_init`). `pico_explorer_base` is the only board with any of them.
- `6b9e776e5` ("Final? update", 2024-10-17) removed the program bytes.

Also correct: no coherent testing/bring-up strategy for rp2x PIO today.

Closest existing coverage: #5141 (RP2350 PIO + CYW43439 gSPI + DMA, hw-tested). That's the nearest thing we have, not a solution.

I'll draft a PIO test plan (unit + hw-in-loop).

Five PIO driver defects, none affecting in-tree callers today: `set_fifo_join` could never join RX FIFO and couldn't undo a join; `add_program` panicked above 16 instructions and on odd byte counts; three of four PIO interrupt lines were never dispatched; block IRQ flags went to the wrong client and could hang the kernel. - unfixed: client on SM0 was called

prs.thread:
### Pull Request Overview

This PR supersedes #5154.

Splicing an app into the kernel breaks the relevant make target on 4 of the 5 RP2 boards: "ELF contains memory contents for uninitialized memory at 20000000". BFD re-lays headers after --set-section-flags .apps=LOAD,ALLOC, and .stack (NOLOAD) ends up claiming file contents for SRAM. Add -R .stack to each objcopy splice rule. Fixes #4770.

<details>
<summary>AI-generated measurement data</summary>

https://via-balaena.github.io/tock-rp2350/findings/4770/

</details>

### Testing Strategy

potto216's RP2040: reporter verified on his machine via program/elf2uf2-rs/BOOTSEL. App ran; console "Hello world!". (https://github.com/tock/tock/issues/4770#issuecomment-5573463328)

program-openocd on RP2350: Pico 2 W over Debug Probe. rc=2 → rc=0. Without fix, openocd verify_image fails at 0x20000000 and aborts before reset, leaving board halted.

File-level: all 4 boards pass (raspberry_pi_pico, raspberry_pi_pico_2, pico_explorer_base, nano_rp2040_connect). pico_explorer_base and nano_rp2040_connect are file-level only. No hardware run yet.

### TODO or Help Wanted

program-probe (probe-rs): not run. Could someone with an RP2040 and probe-rs try it? @potto216 ?

### Checklist

- [x] Ran `make prepush`.

### PR Contents

#### Documentation

- [ ] Updated the relevant files in `/docs` and the [Book](https://github.com/tock/book).
- [x] No documentation updates are required.

#### AI Use

- [ ] No AI was used in this PR.
- [x] AI was used in this PR. I have read [Tock's AI policy](https://github.com/tock/tock/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-policy) and have properly disclosed my AI use below. This PR comment, and any subsequent PR interactions must not be generated using AI, except for under a `<details>` drawer.

Code written with Claude Opus 5
 ␟ > I would rather see this move to use `tockloader local-board`, but if this improves things then fine.

@bradjc 

I can look into that for a future pr. This fixes the immediate breakage. ␟ --set-section-flags .apps=LOAD,ALLOC gives .apps file content, which forces BFD to recompute the program headers. 

.stack is (NOLOAD) and lives in SRAM at 0x20000000; during that recompute its p_filesz changes from 0x0 to its full size. The ELF then claims file content for memory that has none, and elf2uf2-rs refuses it with:
Error: "ELF contains memory contents for uninitialized memory at 20000000"
-R .stack drops it from the flashed artifact only. The kernel ELF keeps its symbols, and .stack reserves stack space with no bytes to carry, so it costs nothing.

The section itself stays NOBITS in the section table; the issue is in the program header (p_filesz), which is why it's not obvious from reading the section headers alone. ␟ > .stack is (NOLOAD) and lives in SRAM at 0x20000000; during that recompute its p_filesz changes from 0x0 to its full size.

Got it. Doesn't this sound like a linker bug? Why does the linker change the `p_filesz` segment header for a `NOLOAD` segment, effectively materializing its contents out of thin air?

Again, not disagreeing with this fix, just trying to fully understand the issue.

commits.messageHeadline: rp2350: build the flashed image with tockloader, not by splicing an ELF
rp2040: the same image route, and one UF2 converter instead of two

prs.thread:
### Pull Request Overview

Fixes two defects in the current flash route:
- #4770: `objcopy` lays the program headers out again; the (NOLOAD) `.stack` segment claims file content for SRAM.
- Ghost app: the splice writes nothing at the slot after the last app, so an old TBF header survives. This route fixes it because `tockloader` writes a terminator at that slot; the loader's existing behavior (stopping at the first invalid header) then prevents the stale app from running.

This route opens no ELF, so #4770 cannot recur. Tockloader builds a flat flash image; picotool/openocd/probe-rs write it directly.

**User-visible:** Apps are now installed with `tockloader install --local-board <tab>`, then `make flash`. `elf2uf2-rs` leaves the tree; `picotool` is used on all five boards (including `raspberry_pi_pico_w`, whose kernel region is 576 KiB and app prog is at `0x10090000`, not `0x10040000`). No Rust changes; 2 commits, Makefiles and READMEs only (four READMEs changed; `raspberry_pi_pico_w/README.md` points readers to the Pico's guide and needed no edit).

**Capability gain:** `--update-section .apps=<file>` takes one file, so the splice route cannot place two apps at all. This route does: `tockloader install --local-board` is called once with both `.tab` files (the signature is `[tab ...]`), then `make flash`. The image is 274,433 bytes. Tockloader's layout reports `leak_claim` (4,096 bytes) at slot `0x10040000` and `leak_observe` (8,192 bytes) at slot `0x10041000`; the kernel lists both. Verified on silicon over SWD and BOOTSEL.

**Conflicts:** #5156 (all four Makefiles) - merge-tested against current head; #5158 is now merged (this branch is rebased onto it; the two README lines this PR replaces are resolved); #5141 merges clean. 

### Testing Strategy

**On the board (Pico 2 W, Debug Probe):**
- `make flash-openocd` runs; process console lists the app live.
- Kernel-only: application region erased first over SWD (`flash erase_address 0x10040000 0x40000`, so the test measures the boot and not a stale app), then `make init` + `make flash-openocd` with nothing installed. Image exactly 262,144 bytes, `** Verified OK **`. Board boots; `list` returns its header row with nothing under it.
- BOOTSEL: UF2 (549,376 bytes, 1,073 blocks, family `0xe48bff59`) copied onto the RP2350 bootloader volume; board left BOOTSEL on its own and both apps came up.
- probe-rs: `probe-rs download --chip RP235x --binary-format bin --base-address 0x10000000` finished in 17.74s, then `probe-rs reset`; board boots.
- Two apps: kernel lists both; the invocation is described above in Capability gain.
- 8,192-byte app then 1,024-byte app, no erase: only the second loads.
- The one-byte A/B test: without the terminator, the kernel runs an app that is not in the image.
- The terminator byte (`flash fillb 0x10041000 0x00 1`) alone invalidates the version field (02→00) and kills the ghost app on reset; the erase that also occurs in the normal flash path is not required to fix the issue.

**On the machine:**
- Pico 2 (RP2350), single-app build: UF2 1,029 blocks, family `0xe48bff59`, payload byte-identical to the image that booted.
- Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040), `elf2uf2-rs` vs `picotool` on the same ELF: 400 blocks, same 102,400 addresses, zero disagreements.
- On the RP2040 image, `picotool` writes 159,744 bytes more, all zero, below the app address.
- Kernel-only UF2: Pico 204,800 → 524,288; Pico 2 147,456 → 524,288. Every added block is zero; every shared block is byte-identical.
- `make init` and `make flash` run end-to-end on `raspberry_pi_pico` with tockloader 1.18.1 and picotool. With tockloader absent, `make flash` exits 2 at `write-kernel` with Error 127.

**Limits:**
- No RP2040 booted. `probe-rs` was verified with `--chip RP235x`; `--chip rp2040` was not exercised.
- The probe-rs invocation is manual (there is no `flash-probe` target on the Pico 2) and matches the Makefile's flag form.

When building app for RPi Pico I get the error: "ELF contains memory contents for uninitialized memory at 20000000". An example is:
```bash
(tools) user@rpi05-dev001:~/tockos/tock/boards/raspberry_pi_pico $ APP=/home/user/tockos/libtock-rs/target/raspberry_pi_pico/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/examples/spi_controller_write_read.tbf  make program
    Finished `release` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.12s
   text    data     bss     dec     hex filename
  98348       0   14364  112712   1b848 /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico
arm-none-eabi-objcopy --set-section-flags .apps=LOAD,ALLOC /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico.elf /home/user/tockos/tock//target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf
arm-none-eabi-objcopy: /home/user/tockos/tock//target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf: section .relocate lma 0x20000000 adjusted to 0x20001500
arm-none-eabi-objcopy --update-section .apps=/home/user/tockos/libtock-rs/target/raspberry_pi_pico/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/examples/spi_controller_write_read.tbf /home/user/tockos/tock//target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf
elf2uf2-rs /home/user/tockos/tock//target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.uf2
Error: "ELF contains memory contents for uninitialized memory at 20000000"
make: *** [Makefile:48: program] Error 1
```

Gemini suggested root cause of elf2uf2-rs tool's error message "uninitialized memory at 20000000" is that the elf2uf2-rs utility is designed to create a flashable image and does not deal with RAM which starts at 0x20000000 on the Raspberry Pi Pico.

Its suggested solution worked for me, which is:
```bash
APP=/home/user/tockos/libtock-rs/target/raspberry_pi_pico/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/examples/spi_controller_write_read.tbf make /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf

arm-none-eabi-objcopy -R .stack -R .relocate -R .bss /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf

elf2uf2-rs /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.elf /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.uf2

cp /home/user/tockos/tock/target/thumbv6m-none-eabi/release/raspberry_pi_pico-app.uf2 /media/user/RPI-RP2/
```
Then I was able to verify the application ran with `tockloader listen --board raspberry_pi_pico --openocd`

findings.body: The Raspberry PI Pico RP2040 USB CDC ACM serial port does not work with many machines # Description The Raspberry PI Pico RP2040 Tock USB CDC ACM serial port implementation does not work with many machines. All Windows 11 Dell and HP Envy laptops I tried reported a Unknown USB Device (Set Address Failed). Their firmware is up to date. It does work with a Windows 11 GMKtec mini PC. It is randomly recognized by a Raspberry Pi 4 and once recognized works fine as a serial port. It does not work with the Raspberry Pi 5. I applied the eeprom updates for the Raspberry Pi. On all machines the RP 2040's firmware programming mode with the USB drive always works. When I capture the physical USB line traffic between the RP 2040 and most computers (Windows/Raspberry Pi) I see a violation of the USB 2.0 control-transfer data-toggle rules, specifically Sections 8.5.3 and 8.6.1 (I'm looking at Revision 2.0 April 27, 2000). For a control read/write as shown in Figure 8-37 after a valid SETUP transaction for the IN transaction DATA must be toggled by the device to DATA1. But as shown below the RP2040 is incorrectly using DATA0. Additionally the RP2040 sends the wrong amount of data for the GET_DESCRIPTOR request. The RP2040 should only send 18 bytes as specified by the spec (Table 9-8. Standard Device Descriptor), but instead it is sending 64 bytes on the first IN transaction. Then it sends a second IN with the correct 18 bytes. This happens on the Windows 11 machines and on the Raspberry Pis when they fail. Expanded 2nd IN with correct 18 bytes: This matches when the GET_DESCRIPTION does work and both DATA1 is correct and only one IN is correctly sent (below) Does anyone have any thoughts on this. I'm not familiar with developing or debugging device side USB interfaces. Currently I'm debugging the issue based on OpenAI's analysis below but I don't have the skill to judge if it is reasonable or not. thanks! # OpenAI analysis The Pico sends a 64-byte DATA0 packet on endpoint zero immediately after the SETUP transaction. Two details make this a smoking gun: 1. The first data or status packet after a control SETUP must use DATA1, not DATA0. 2. The packet length of exactly 64 bytes matches a hard-coded value in Tock’s RP2040 bus-reset handler. The host ACKs the DATA0 packet but apparently discards it as having the wrong data toggle, then retries the IN transaction. That behavior is consistent with duplicate/wrong-toggle handling: the receiver ACKs so the sender does not retransmit forever, but does not accept the packet as the expected DATA1 transaction. Tock’s current RP2040 USB driver does this during bus reset: ```rust self.dpsram.ep_buf_ctrl[0].ep_in_buf_ctrl.modify( EP_BUFFER_CONTROL::AVAILABLE0::SET + EP_BUFFER_CONTROL::TRANSFER_LENGTH0.val(64) + EP_BUFFER_CONTROL::DATA_PID0::CLEAR, ); ``` That gives the RP2040 USB controller ownership of EP0 IN with: ``` AVAILABLE = 1 length = 64 PID = DATA0 ``` That is exactly what appears in packet 140: DATA0-BAD Data(64 bytes) The setup-request path subsequently tries to configure the first control-read packet as DATA1. It sets next_pid_in to 1 and calls transmit_in_ep0(). The transmission function then attempts to replace the length and PID and finally sets AVAILABLE. But AVAILABLE was already set by handle_bus_reset(). The USB controller already owns that buffer and can read it concurrently while the CPU modifies the length, PID, and contents. The RP2040 datasheet explicitly warns against this. It says USB DPRAM is asynchronous and non-atomic, and software must: 1. write the buffer information; 2. wait enough system-clock cycles for a USB-clock cycle; 3. set AVAILABLE separately and last. This ensures that the controller cannot observe AVAILABLE=1 with stale length or PID information. The capture appears to show that exact race: the controller observes the old reset values—64 bytes and DATA0—instead of the newly prepared descriptor response—probably 18 bytes and DATA1.

findings.body:
### Pull Request Overview

Fixes two defects in the current flash route:
- #4770: `objcopy` lays the program headers out again; the (NOLOAD) `.stack` segment claims file content for SRAM.
- Ghost app: the splice writes nothing at the slot after the last app, so an old TBF header survives. This route fixes it because `tockloader` writes a terminator at that slot; the loader's existing behavior (stopping at the first invalid header) then prevents the stale app from running.

This route opens no ELF, so #4770 cannot recur. Tockloader builds a flat flash image; picotool/openocd/probe-rs write it directly.

**User-visible:** Apps are now installed with `tockloader install --local-board <tab>`, then `make flash`. `elf2uf2-rs` leaves the tree; `picotool` is used on all five boards (including `raspberry_pi_pico_w`, whose kernel region is 576 KiB and app prog is at `0x10090000`, not `0x10040000`). No Rust changes; 2 commits, Makefiles and READMEs only (four READMEs changed; `raspberry_pi_pico_w/README.md` points readers to the Pico's guide and needed no edit).

**Capability gain:** `--update-section .apps=<file>` takes one file, so the splice route cannot place two apps at all. This route does: `tockloader install --local-board` is called once with both `.tab` files (the signature is `[tab ...]`), then `make flash`. The image is 274,433 bytes. Tockloader's layout reports `leak_claim` (4,096 bytes) at slot `0x10040000` and `leak_observe` (8,192 bytes) at slot `0x10041000`; the kernel lists both. Verified on silicon over SWD and BOOTSEL.

**Conflicts:** #5156 (all four Makefiles) - merge-tested against current head; #5158 is now merged (this branch is rebased onto it; the two README lines this PR replaces are resolved); #5141 merges clean. 

### Testing Strategy

**On the board (Pico 2 W, Debug Probe):**
- `make flash-openocd` runs; process console lists the app live.
- Kernel-only: application region erased first over SWD (`flash erase_address 0x10040000 0x40000`, so the test measures the boot and not a stale app), then `make init` + `make flash-openocd` with nothing installed. Image exactly 262,144 bytes, `** Verified OK **`. Board boots; `list` returns its header row with nothing under it.
- BOOTSEL: UF2 (549,376 bytes, 1,073 blocks, family `0xe48bff59`) copied onto the RP2350 bootloader volume; board left BOOTSEL on its own and both apps came up.
- probe-rs: `probe-rs download --chip RP235x --binary-format bin --base-address 0x10000000` finished in 17.74s, then `probe-rs reset`; board boots.
- Two apps: kernel lists both; the invocation is described above in Capability gain.
- 8,192-byte app then 1,024-byte app, no erase: only the second loads.
- The one-byte A/B test: without the terminator, the kernel runs an app that is not in the image.
- The terminator byte (`flash fillb 0x10041000 0x00 1`) alone invalidates the version field (02→00) and kills the ghost app on reset; the erase that also occurs in the normal flash path is not required to fix the issue.

**On the machine:**
- Pico 2 (RP2350), single-app build: UF2 1,029 blocks, family `0xe48bff59`, payload byte-identical to the image that booted.
- Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040), `elf2uf2-rs` vs `picotool` on the same ELF: 400 blocks, same 102,400 addresses, zero disagreements.
- On the RP2040 image, `picotool` writes 159,744 bytes more, all zero, below the app address.
- Kernel-only UF2: Pico 204,800 → 524,288; Pico 2 147,456 → 524,288. Every added block is zero; every shared block is byte-identical.
- `make init` and `make flash` run end-to-end on `raspberry_pi_pico` with tockloader 1.18.1 and picotool. With tockloader absent, `make flash` exits 2 at `write-kernel` with Error 127.

**Limits:**
- No RP2040 booted. `probe-rs` was verified with `--chip RP235x`; `--chip rp2040` was not exercised.
- The probe-rs invocation is manual (there is no `flash-probe` target on the Pico 2) and matches the Makefile's flag form.
